acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Crocodilians family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Mire Caiman, T1, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Waterline Initiate archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two normal construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Small low caiman with mottled hide, narrow juvenile scutes, compact jaw, and thin tail.
Signature mechanic: V-Wake Snap: the Caiman's eyes sink but its wake points continuously toward the fixed bank endpoint.
battlefieldDuty: Submerge along one visible ripple and snap once at the bank.
constructionDimensions: Hide, scutes, mud, algae, teeth, claws, saliva, and water wakes remain natural and materially distinct.
Submersion and rotation read through eye position, coherent wakes, tail curve, bank grooves, and exposed belly.
counterplay: Move parallel to the bank and punish the exposed tail after the missed snap. Affinity signal: The V wake, foreclaw grooves, tapping jaw tip, locked side scutes, or ordered channel strike remains visible before commitment.
forbiddenTreatments: Humanoid posture, tools, clothing, or armor
Wings, breath weapons, or draconic horns
identityInvariants: Every form retains a low four-legged crocodilian body, long tail, scuted back, belly fault, sensory pits, and a jaw-driven attack silhouette.
Tier escalation uses snout geometry, scute height, neck mobility, tail mass, scars, and waterline behavior rather than equipment or wings.
Eyes, wake direction, jaw angle, foreclaw grooves, tail curve, and exposed belly keep ambush and rotation counterplay readable.
telegraph: The eyes submerge while a narrow V-shaped wake remains visible.
